label: Has building graphics
summary: Whether the culture uses the given building graphics set.
details: Works on a culture. Vanilla writes a building graphics name such as `iranian_building_gfx` or `norse_building_gfx`.

label: Has building (or upgrade)
summary: Whether the province has the given building, or a later upgrade of it.
details: Works on a province. Vanilla writes the first level of a building line, such as `paddy_fields_01`; the game's documentation says a successor (upgrade) of the named building also counts.

label: Has building with flag
summary: Whether the province has a building that carries the given flag.
details: Works on a province. A flag is a tag that building definitions can carry, so one check covers every building with it. Written as a single name it means at least one such building. The block form can ask for a number of them with `count >= 2`.

fields.name: flag
fields.text: The building flag to look for.
fields.values: a building flag name, such as `travel_point_of_interest_martial`

fields.name: count
fields.text: How many matching buildings are needed, written as a comparison such as `count >= 2`.

label: Has casus belli on
summary: Whether the character has the given casus belli (a valid reason for war) against the target character.
details: Works on a character. If the target is not valid, the check is simply false. Vanilla writes the casus belli either as `cb` or as `casus_belli`; both are used.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character the casus belli would be used against.

fields.name: cb
fields.text: The casus belli to look for. `casus_belli` is accepted in the same place.
fields.values: a casus belli key, such as `claim_cb`

label: Has character flag
summary: Whether the character has the given flag set on them.
details: Works on a character. Flags are markers that script sets elsewhere and reads back with this check. Vanilla mostly writes the flag name directly, and sometimes a scope reference.

label: Has character modifier
summary: Whether the character currently has the named modifier.
details: Works on a character. Write the modifier key, such as `gangrene_modifier`.

label: Character modifier time left
summary: Checks the time remaining on a named modifier of the character.
details: The game's documentation gives only the form `has_character_modifier_duration_remaining = name` and no comparison or unit, and vanilla does not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has nominated successor
summary: Whether the given character has nominated a successor for this elective title.
details: Works on a title with elective succession (the holder is chosen by electors). The key is spelled `nominiated` in the game. Vanilla uses it once, with `root` as the character.

label: Claim on
summary: Whether the character holds an explicit claim on the given title.
details: Works on a character. The game's documentation says it checks for an explicit claim. Vanilla usually passes a title in a scope such as `prev` or `scope:title`.

label: Has clerical region
summary: Whether the title belongs to a clerical region.
details: Works on a title. `yes` checks that it has one, `no` that it has none. The input does not say what a clerical region is beyond its name.

label: Clerical region in realm
summary: Whether the character's realm contains counties of the given clerical region.
details: Works on a character. The value is the title of the clerical region, usually held in a saved scope.

label: Has clothing graphics
summary: Whether the culture uses the given clothing graphics set.
details: Works on a culture. Vanilla writes names such as `indian_clothing_gfx`. The game's documentation example wrongly shows `has_building_gfx`; the key to write is `has_clothing_gfx`.

label: Has coat of arms graphics
summary: Whether the culture uses the given coat of arms graphics set.
details: Works on a culture. Vanilla writes names such as `norse_coa_gfx` or `arabic_group_coa_gfx`. The game's documentation example wrongly shows `has_building_gfx`; the key to write is `has_coa_gfx`.

label: Has coastal province
summary: Whether the county contains a coastal province.
details: Works on a county title. Vanilla uses it with `yes` only.

label: Has cohesion
summary: Whether the confederation or bloc has a cohesion value.
details: Works on a confederation (a bloc of rulers). The game's documentation does not explain when one has none. Vanilla uses it three times, always with `yes`.

label: Cohesion level parameter
summary: Whether the confederation or bloc's current cohesion level carries the given parameter.
details: Only the level the bloc is on right now is looked at. Vanilla writes parameter names such as `any_member_activity_cost_reduced`.

label: Completed activity intent
summary: Whether the character has completed an intent of the given type in the activity they are involved in.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses activity intent keys such as `woo_attendee_intent`. Written as a single name it checks that intent type. The block form can also name a target.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The intent type to look for.
fields.values: an activity intent key, such as `woo_attendee_intent`

fields.name: target
fields.text: Only count the intent if it was aimed at this character.

label: Has completed inspiration
summary: Whether the character has ever completed an inspiration.
details: `yes` means at least once in their life; `no` means never.

label: Constructing building with flag
summary: Whether the province is currently constructing a building that has the given flag.
details: Works on a province. It looks at buildings under construction, not finished ones; use the building flag check for those. Vanilla writes flags such as `temple`, `castle`, `city` and `tribe`.

label: Has contact
summary: Whether the checked character has the given character as a contact.
details: The game's documentation words it as checking whether someone has the character as an employer and explains nothing more. Vanilla uses it with faction members, such as `scope:faction.faction_leader`.

label: Has council
summary: Whether the character has a council.
details: Takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla does not use it in the input data.

label: Council position
summary: Whether the character holds the given position on a council.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla writes councillor types such as `councillor_marshal` or `councillor_court_chaplain`.

label: Has councillor for skill
summary: Whether the character has a councillor for the given skill.
details: Write a skill name or `general`, as the game's documentation says. Vanilla uses it twice, once with `general` and once with a `$SKILL$` placeholder in a template.

label: Has county modifier
summary: Whether the county has the named modifier.
details: Works on a county title. Write the modifier's key, such as `backwater_county_modifier`.

label: County modifier time left
summary: Checks the time remaining on a named modifier of the county.
details: The game's documentation gives only the form `has_county_modifier_duration_remaining = name` and no comparison or unit, and vanilla does not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has county of faith
summary: Whether the ruler has at least one county of the given faith in their realm.
details: The documented example runs it on a ruler (a character) with a faith as the value, but the input lists the faith as the scope it runs in. Check which one the game accepts before relying on it.

label: Court language
summary: Whether the character's court language is the given language.
details: Works on a character. Write a language key, such as `language_norwegian`.

label: Court language of culture
summary: Whether the character's court language is the language of the given culture.
details: Works on a character. The value is a culture, such as `prev.culture` or `culture:han`.

label: Court position
summary: Whether the character holds the given court position.
details: Works on a character. Write a court position type, such as `court_physician_court_position`.

label: Court type
summary: Whether the character's court is of the given type.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla writes types such as `court_diplomatic`, `court_intrigue` and `court_warlike`.

label: Cultural era (or later)
summary: Whether the culture has reached the given era or a later one.
details: Works on a culture. Vanilla writes eras such as `culture_era_early_medieval`, `culture_era_high_medieval` and `culture_era_late_medieval`.

label: Cultural parameter
summary: Whether the culture has the given cultural parameter switched on.
details: Works on a culture. Vanilla uses it with many parameter names, such as `unlock_maa_cataphract_archers` or `next_level_fortification`.

label: Cultural pillar
summary: Whether the culture has the given pillar, such as a heritage or a language.
details: Works on a culture. Vanilla mostly uses it with heritages, for example `heritage_byzantine`.

label: Cultural tradition
summary: Whether the culture has the given tradition.
details: Works on a culture. Write a tradition key such as `tradition_hunters`, or a scope that holds one (vanilla uses `prev` this way).

label: Has culture
summary: Whether the character has the given culture.
details: Works on a character. Write a culture such as `culture:norse`, or a scope that holds one.

label: Current phase
summary: Whether the activity is currently in the given phase.
details: Works on an activity. Activities run in phases, such as the joust or the melee in a tournament. Write the phase key, such as `tournament_phase_joust`.

label: Has custom title name
summary: Whether the title uses a custom name set by script.
details: Works on a title. A title gets a custom name through `set_title_name` or `set_random_dynasty_title_name`.

label: De jure claim on
summary: Whether the character has a de jure claim against the target.
details: The game's documentation says the target is a character, and vanilla does not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Dead character has flag
summary: Whether the dead character has the given flag.
details: Like the normal character flag check, but for a character who has died. Vanilla uses it once.

label: Dead character has variable
summary: Whether the dead character has the given variable.
details: Like the normal variable check, but for a character who has died. Vanilla uses it for things such as `body_has_been_disposed`.
